subject.title: Conversational agent lane wedges indefinitely: ingress events never reconcile (re-delivery storm on reconnect) + abort_embedded_run leaves owner lock unreleased (released=0)

question: After current-release evidence confirms the remaining WhatsApp ingress behavior, should OpenClaw add an operator-facing inspect/drain mechanism in addition to a bounded automatic replay policy?
rationale: The core correctness question is reproducible behavior, but the requested raw-queue recovery verb and replay-age policy determine a new operator-facing product contract.

options.title: First prove and fix completion/replay
options.body: Require a current-release capture of pending records after normally completed runs, then implement the narrow durable-ingress correction without adding a new operator command yet.

options.title: Add recovery tooling too
options.body: Pair the correctness fix with a supported journal inspection and drain/ack workflow for operators recovering poison records.

options.title: Treat replay policy as plugin-owned
options.body: Keep generic durable-journal semantics narrow and let the WhatsApp plugin own any channel-specific replay threshold or recovery UX.

recommendation.title: First prove and fix completion/replay
recommendation.body: Require a current-release capture of pending records after normally completed runs, then implement the narrow durable-ingress correction without adding a new operator command yet.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged run-lifecycle work and follow-up analysis connect the lane-release invariant to this issue's remaining ingress boundary.
